content.title: Who is the new pope? More on the first American pope and his ties to Villanova
content.text: May 8, 2025, 2:54 p.m. ETCardinal Robert Francis Prevost, an American, has been elected as the 267th pope, taking the name Leo XIV.The 69-year-old new pope is a Chicago native, Villanova University alumnus and Augustinian priest.Reactions to the historic election have poured in from religious leaders and politicians.White smoke came from the chimney of the Sistine Chapel on Thursday, signaling the selection of not only a new pope, but the first American pope: Cardinal Robert Francis Prevost.Members of the papal conclave selected the American to serve as the 267th pope. He will take the name Leo XIV. He also has significant ties to the local area as a Villanova University alumnus.Here's more about Pope Leo XIV, the papal conclave and local reactions to the new pope.Who is the new pope?Pope Leo XIV is a Chicago native and Augustinian priest.He was elected via conclave May 8 to serve as the 267th pope of the Roman Catholic church.How old is the pope?Pope Leo XIV is 69 years old.Pope Francis, who died April 21, was 76-years-old when he was elected in 2013.Pope Leo XIV VillanovaThe new pope graduated from Villanova University in 1977. This university is the only Augustinian Catholic university in the U.S.Those at the university during the conclave's selection shared what the scene from the campus looked like.NJ reactions to the new popeBishop David M. O'Connell of the Trenton Diocese reacted to the election of an American Pope via the diocese's newsletter."Today, the Diocese of Trenton rejoices and gives thanks to God for the election of our new Holy Father, Pope Leo XIV. This momentous occasion marks the beginning of a new chapter in the life of the Church, filled with hope and renewed commitment to our faith," O'Connell wrote.Local politicians and lawmakers also responded swiftly to the news."Today, Catholics around the world are beaming with pride as His Holiness Pope Leo XIV makes history as the first American pope," New Jersey Gov. Phil Murphy said in a statement."Tammy and I are praying for Pope Leo XIV's enduring success as he becomes the spiritual leader for more than one billion Roman Catholics around the world — including myself."U.S. Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ) and U.S. Rep. Jeff Van Drew (R-NJ) also reacted to the news on the social media platform X."It is powerful and promising to hear Pope Leo XIV's words of peace and humility be some of his first in this role. ... We live in difficult times of uncertainty and conflict, and we need powerful voices calling for dignity and decency in our humanity," Kim wrote.Van Drew offered his congratulations to the new pope."I am praying for Pope Leo XIV as he takes on the incredible responsibility of leading 1.4 billion Catholics around the world," Van Drew added.Kaitlyn McCormick writes about trending issues and community news across South Jersey for the Courier-Post, The Daily Journal and the Burlington County Times.
